    </div>

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    For each skill, score your team today and the level it needs under agentic delivery; record the gap and choose exactly one action: hire, train or accept. If you choose train, name a track from block F. Then redline the hiring loop and assign an owner to every decision.

  <div class="ws-block">
    <h2>E &mdash; The team composition target
      <span class="ws-block-note">book priors and our figures are separate; projections are directional, not prescriptive</span></h2>
    <div class="prior--hedged">
      <span class="hedge-figure">Typical team size: 4–7 engineers † &nbsp; | &nbsp; Senior-to-junior ratio: 1:1 to 2:1 † &nbsp; | &nbsp; Context engineering allocation: 10–20% of team capacity † &nbsp; | &nbsp; Review time allocation: 25–35% of team capacity †</span>
      <span class="hedge-text">† Projected figures are based on early adopter reports and the author's observations, not longitudinal studies. Pre-agentic figures reflect established industry norms.</span>
      <span class="hedge-src">handbook\ch06-team-structures.qmd L308-315</span>
    </div>
    <div class="prior">
      <b>These are directional, not prescriptive.</b> Your ratios depend on codebase complexity, agent maturity, and domain risk. A team working on a payments system with strict regulatory requirements will need a higher senior ratio than a team building internal tooling.
      <br><b>Smaller does not mean fewer total engineers.</b> Agent-augmented teams produce more per person, but the economic argument is not "we need fewer engineers." It is "we need the same or fewer engineers to do more, with a different mix of skills." The staffing question is about composition and capability, not reduction.
      <span class="prior-src">ch06 L319-321</span>
    </div>
    <div class="prior"><b>Dagger footnote and caveats:</b> the dagger disclosure and both caveats above apply to all four profile-matched priors. The figures are directional, not prescriptive; the ratio depends on codebase complexity, agent maturity and domain risk, and smaller does not mean fewer total engineers.<span class="prior-src">ch06 L315, L319-321</span></div>
